summary.text: A male infant born at term by caesarean section after an uneventful pregnancy, with no tachycardia noted at earlier checkups, attended a scheduled checkup at 111 days of age where marked tachycardia was detected and he was referred the same day. Parents reported occasional irregular breathing after feeding; he was active and feeding well. Family history was negative.

On admission the ventricular rate fluctuated between 160 and 240 beats/min, with massive cardiomegaly (CTR 0.66) and narrow QRS tachycardia. Echocardiography showed a severely dilated left ventricle with diffuse hypokinesis and LVEF approximately 20%, and NT-proBNP was markedly elevated. Infectious and metabolic work-up was negative. ATP unmasked sawtooth flutter waves, confirming atrial flutter with tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy.

Synchronized cardioversion at 1 J/kg restored sinus rhythm immediately. Heart failure therapy with milrinone, furosemide, fluid restriction, spironolactone, carvedilol and temporary low-dose aspirin followed; no anticoagulation or antiarrhythmic prophylaxis was given.

The cardiothoracic ratio fell to 0.55 by Day 12 and on Day 18 LVDd was 34 mm with normalized LVEF and resolved mitral regurgitation. He was discharged home on Day 25, aspirin was later stopped, and at 10-month follow-up he was asymptomatic with normalized echocardiography and NT-proBNP and no arrhythmia on Holter monitoring.
